coefficient.description: Normalized correlation coefficient [-1, 1] under the selected method

mechanism: A normalized measure of statistical association between two {{variable}}s under a selected correlation method. The coefficient lies in [-1, 1] and is interpreted according to that method. Correlation alone neither establishes nor rules out {{causation}}, its direction, or an intervention effect.
gloss: Normalized statistical association; no causal conclusion by itself
invariants: The correlation alone establishes neither the presence nor absence of {{causation}}, its direction, nor an intervention effect, regardless of coefficient magnitude.
failure_modes: Causal overreach: the result alone is used to assert a causal relation, its absence or direction, or an intervention effect.
Source ambiguity: direct causation, reverse causation, confounding, and selection can produce similar coefficients, which correlation alone cannot distinguish.
Method blindness: dependence outside the selected method's sensitivity yields a weak coefficient that is read as independence.
